audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3, Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items are all marked Gragas in the full layer but carry Akshan-favoured boilerplate — "trades start at angles melee kits literally cannot answer", "take over the lane and start roaming for revives".
audit.why: At 31.58% over 19 games this is the second-worst matchup in the slice, and the content layer explains why: Body Slam at 3 stuns through Heroic Swing and he simply out-brawls you afterwards. The full layer's stage text was never reconciled with its own sides.
audit.corrected: The four stages now name what owns them — Body Slam's 14s dash-stun at 3, Drunken Rage's flat 5s in the 4-5 window, his AP-bruiser item eating your burst, and the Body Slam into Explosive Cask one-shot at two items.

audit.why: Spikes are right on both sides: Akshan at 1-2 before Body Slam exists, Gragas at 3, Akshan at 6 with Comeuppance (100/85/70), Gragas at two items. Explosive Cask is also 100/85/70, which is why the level-6 window is genuinely contested.

audit.whatIsWrong: Happy Hour is absent from the entire page — Gragas's passive is never mentioned in either layer. Drunken Rage is described as something to bait or play around, with no cooldown given, and dosFull[2] called a whiffed Body Slam a "fifteen-second invitation".
audit.why: Happy Hour heals Gragas periodically whenever he uses a skill, which is why chip poke does not accumulate on him — that is the reason the itemization line's anti-heal actually matters here, and the page never connected the two. Drunken Rage is a flat 5s cooldown, so there is no meaningful downtime to bait: the advice has to be out-spacing it, not waiting it out. Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, not fifteen.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour is now stated in the early text, the level-3 spike and whys[1]; Drunken Rage carries its flat 5s so the reader stops trying to bait it; Body Slam's 14s rank-1 cooldown replaces the fifteen-second figure and is stated across the cooldown block, do's, don'ts and the interactions report.

edits.before: Short trades, disciplined swings, and the execute when his kit is down. Keep one eye on Body Slam and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Short trades, disciplined swings, and the execute when his kit is down. Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 — that is the only clock.

edits.before: Full kit: E swing around terrain fires while moving — trades start at angles melee kits literally cannot answer.
edits.after: Body Slam at 3 is a 14s dash-stun that interrupts Heroic Swing outright — your angles stop being safe.

edits.before: Trade on his CS timings and bank the passive shield-sprints. Track Body Slam; the swing dies to one good answer.
edits.after: Trade on his CS timings, but Drunken Rage is a flat 5s — you cannot wait his damage reduction out, only out-space it.

edits.before: First item spike — the swing-fire pattern now removes half bars. Take over the lane and start roaming for revives.
edits.after: His AP-bruiser first item adds HP and AP that eat your Youmuu's burst while Drunken Rage blunts the rest.

edits.before: Crit items even out the field — your edge stays the map game: revives, executes, and swings nobody wards.
edits.after: Body Slam into Explosive Cask one-shots a shieldless you — your edge is the map: picks, revives, roams.

edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, his engage and escape in one button, and it stuns through your swing. - E swing is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.after: His engage and his escape in one button, 14s at rank 1 — that downtime is the green light, so wait for it.

edits.after: Gragas E Body Slam comes online at 14s — his biggest threat window. The dash-stun interrupts Heroic Swing, and Happy Hour heals him on every cast.

edits.before: Gragas shrugs your Avengerang poke with W damage reduction on a large health bar, so your early chip barely dents him.
edits.after: Drunken Rage is a flat 5s so he blunts every Avengerang, and Happy Hour heals him on each cast — early chip barely dents him.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are your window: Gragas has no gap-closer until his E Body Slam at 3, so he has to walk into your Avengerang range to last-hit. Land the boomerang and your double-shot passive, cancel the second shot for the move speed, and reset spacing before he can touch you. The catch is he barely cares about your poke — he drinks W (Drunken Rage) for flat damage reduction and just absorbs the chip on his big HP bar, and unlike most squishies he has no obligation to trade back early. The instant he hits 3 and has Body Slam, stop sitting at dash range: that E is a stun on impact and it interrupts any Heroic Swing you try.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are your window: Gragas has no gap-closer until his E Body Slam at 3, so he has to walk into your Avengerang range to last-hit. Land the boomerang and your double-shot passive, cancel the second shot for the move speed, and reset spacing before he can touch you. The catch is he barely cares about your poke — Drunken Rage is a flat 5s, so he drinks it for damage reduction on essentially every trade, and Happy Hour heals him each time he casts anything, quietly refunding your chip onto his big HP bar. The instant he hits 3 and has Body Slam, stop sitting at dash range: that E is a 14s stun on impact and it interrupts any Heroic Swing you try.

notes: The page repeatedly tells you to chunk Gragas 'under ~40%' before Comeuppance. Riot's Comeuppance description only says the damage is 'based on missing health' with no threshold or ratio, so the 40% figure is not sourceable from the kit and was left in place rather than changed or asserted — logged as unverified. Explosive Cask knocks back from the blast centre, so the page's 'knocks you into his tower or his team' is achievable by cask placement and was left as written.
